content: Lopinavir interacts with numerous drugs by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. These interactions can lead to increased or decreased drug levels, necessitating careful monitoring and dose adjustments in many cases. Below are specific interactions: 1. Dronabinol: As a CYP3A4 substrate, its levels may increase when co-administered with lopinavir. Caution and monitoring are advised. 2. Dronedarone: Increases lopinavir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 3. Duvelisib: Lopinavir increases duvelisib levels, potentially raising the risk of toxicities. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 4. Efavirenz: Decreases lopinavir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 5. Elagolix: Lopinavir increases elagolix levels, requiring therapy modification and close monitoring. Co-administration of elagolix with strong CYP3A inhibitors for more than one month is not recommended. 6. Eluxadoline: Lopinavir increases eluxadoline levels by affecting CYP2D6 metabolism. Due to incomplete information on eluxadoline metabolism, caution is advised when co-administered with strong CYP2D6 inhibitors. 7. Elvitegravir: Lopinavir significantly increases elvitegravir levels. The recommended dose of elvitegravir is 85 mg once daily when co-administered with lopinavir/ritonavir. 8. Encorafenib: Lopinavir affects encorafenib metabolism, potentially increasing toxicity or reducing efficacy. Caution and monitoring are required. 9. Enfortumab Vedotin: Lopinavir increases the toxicity of enfortumab vedotin by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 10. Escitalopram: Lopinavir increases escitalopram levels, raising the risk of serotonin syndrome. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 11. Eszopiclone: Lopinavir increases eszopiclone levels. Therapy modification is required, with a reduced starting dose of 1 mg/day. 12. Ethosuximide: Lopinavir increases ethosuximide levels, potentially leading to increased toxicity. Caution and monitoring are advised. 13. Etoposide: Lopinavir increases etoposide levels. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 14. Etrasimod: Both drugs may prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of arrhythmias. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 15. Etravirine: Etravirine decreases lopinavir levels, while lopinavir increases etravirine levels. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 16. Exenatide: Lopinavir decreases the effects of exenatide due to reports of hyperglycemia caused by insulin resistance with protease inhibitors. Caution and monitoring are advised. 17. Ezogabine: Both drugs may increase QTc interval prolongation. QT interval monitoring is recommended. 18. Felodipine: Lopinavir increases felodipine levels. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 19. Fluconazole: Increases lopinavir levels. Caution and monitoring are advised. 20. Fludrocortisone: Decreases lopinavir levels. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 21. Flurazepam: Lopinavir increases flurazepam levels. Therapy modification and monitoring are required, with consideration of alternative benzodiazepines. 22. Fluticasone: Caution and monitoring are necessary. 23. Fluvoxamine: Increases lopinavir levels. Caution and monitoring are advised. 24. Fosamprenavir: Increases lopinavir levels. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 25. Fosaprepitant: Lopinavir increases fosaprepitant levels. Caution and monitoring are required. 26. Fosphenytoin: Decreases lopinavir levels. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 27. Fostamatinib: Lopinavir increases fostamatinib levels. Therapy modification and monitoring are required. 28. Fostemsavir: Both drugs may prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 29. Gefitinib: Lopinavir increases gefitinib levels, raising the risk of adverse effects. Therapy modification and monitoring are required. 30. Gemcitabine: Both drugs may prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 31. Gepirone: Both drugs may prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and monitoring are required. 32. Glyburide: Lopinavir decreases glyburide effects due to reports of hyperglycemia caused by insulin resistance with protease inhibitors. Caution and monitoring are advised. 33. Grapefruit: Increases lopinavir levels. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 34. Griseofulvin: Decreases lopinavir levels. Caution and monitoring are required. 35. Guanfacine: Lopinavir increases guanfacine levels. Therapy modification and monitoring are required, with a recommended dose reduction for extended-release guanfacine. 36. Hydrocodone: Lopinavir increases hydrocodone levels, potentially causing fatal respiratory depression. Therapy modification and monitoring are required. 37. Hydrocortisone: Decreases lopinavir levels. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 38. Idelalisib: Increases lopinavir levels. Therapy modification and monitoring are required. 39. Ifosfamide: Lopinavir decreases ifosfamide efficacy by reducing its active metabolites. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 40. Iloperidone: Increases lopinavir levels. Caution and monitoring are required. 41. Indacaterol: Both drugs may prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 42. Indinavir: Lopinavir increases indinavir levels. Caution and monitoring are required. 43. Insulin (various types): Lopinavir decreases insulin efficacy due to reports of hyperglycemia caused by insulin resistance with protease inhibitors. Caution and monitoring are advised. 44. Isoniazid: Increases lopinavir levels. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 45. Istradefylline: Lopinavir increases istradefylline levels. Therapy modification and monitoring are required. 46. Itraconazole: Increases lopinavir levels. Therapy modification and monitoring are required, with a maximum itraconazole dose of 200 mg/day. 47. Ivacaftor: Lopinavir increases ivacaftor levels. Therapy modification and monitoring are required. 48. Ketamine: Lopinavir decreases ketamine levels. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 49. Ketoconazole: Increases lopinavir levels. Therapy modification and monitoring are required, with a maximum ketoconazole dose of 200 mg/day. 50. Lacosamide: Lopinavir increases lacosamide levels. Therapy modification and monitoring are required. 51. Lamotrigine: Lopinavir decreases lamotrigine levels by 50%. Dose adjustments are necessary. 52. Lapatinib: Increases lopinavir levels. Caution and monitoring are required. 53. Lenacapavir: Increases lopinavir levels. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 54. Lenvatinib: Both drugs may prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are required. 55. Letermovir: Increases lopinavir levels. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 56. Levomilnacipran: Lopinavir increases levomilnacipran levels. Therapy modification and monitoring are required, with a maximum dose of 80 mg/day. 57. Linagliptin: Lopinavir may increase or decrease linagliptin levels. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 58. Liraglutide: Lopinavir decreases liraglutide effects due to reports of hyperglycemia caused by insulin resistance with protease inhibitors. Caution and monitoring are advised. 59. Lofexidine: Both drugs may prolong the QTc interval. ECG monitoring is recommended. 60. Lorlatinib: Decreases lopinavir levels. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 61. Lumacaftor/Ivacaftor: Lopinavir increases lumacaftor/ivacaftor levels. Therapy modification and monitoring are required. 62. Lumataperone: Lopinavir increases lumataperone levels. Therapy modification and monitoring are required. 63. Lopinavir and Mifepristone: Both drugs may prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and monitoring are required. 64. Mirtazapine: Lopinavir increases mirtazapine levels. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 65. Mitotane: Decreases lopinavir levels. Caution and monitoring are required. 66. Mometasone: Lopinavir increases mometasone levels, raising the risk of Cushing's syndrome or adrenal suppression. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 67. Naldemedine: Lopinavir increases naldemedine levels. Caution and monitoring are required. 68. Nateglinide: Lopinavir decreases nateglinide effects due to reports of hyperglycemia caused by insulin resistance with protease inhibitors. Caution and monitoring are advised. 69. Nefazodone: Increases lopinavir levels. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 70. Nelfinavir: Increases lopinavir levels. Caution and monitoring are required. 71. Netupitant/Palonosetron: Lopinavir increases netupitant levels. Therapy modification and monitoring are required. 72. Nevirapine: Decreases lopinavir levels. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 73. Nifedipine: Lopinavir increases nifedipine levels. Caution and monitoring are required. This list highlights the importance of monitoring and adjusting therapy when lopinavir is co-administered with other medications due to its significant impact on CYP3A4 metabolism.
